artifact_role.relationship: This file records category contracts, retag decisions and audit reasoning. Its compact exact_shortlists restate candidates only to justify taxonomy; they are not a second import bundle. Candidate facts, access, scores and import authority remain in the named arcades/trades/faith, street-furniture and dedicated Art Nouveau dossiers.

snapshot.rule: No famousness padding, no generic series members, no private-interior promises, and no production import before the parent run's final collision and source review.

decision.ship_rationale: These are four visually and behaviourally distinct accidental-discovery lenses. The first three emerged from this taxonomy audit; artnouveau was subsequently promoted only after a dedicated 33-lead follow-up produced 11 all-high whole-facade candidates. Each has a strict Paris launch set, a clean boundary from the live registry, and immediate reuse in multiple world cities.

arcades.label: Covered arcades
arcades.definition: A named, publicly traversable roofed or colonnaded pedestrian commercial passage whose surviving route and architecture are the objective.
include: Historic glazed commercial passages and gallerias designed as pedestrian through-routes.
A route with current ordinary public passage during stated hours and an exact named-way or entrance coordinate.
A passage whose roof, paving, shop rhythm or trading history remains legible while walking through it.
exclude: Open-air alleys and lanes, including Cour du Commerce Saint-André.
Modern shopping-mall corridors, station concourses, cloisters and porticoes that are not public commercial through-routes.
An individual business inside the passage; retain its narrower business category when independently strong.

why_existing_categories_fail.alley: Alley describes an open-air lane morphology, not a roofed public interior-street.
why_existing_categories_fail.history: History is too broad to expose the repeatable walk-through form.
why_existing_categories_fail.market: Market is about recurring trade, while an arcade remains the objective even when its tenant mix changes.

global_reuse: Milan, Turin, Naples and Genoa gallerias

streetfurniture.label: Street furniture
streetfurniture.definition: An individually distinctive human-scale object installed in public space to provide recurring civic service, information, measurement, comfort or access.
include: A last, first, protected, one-off, custom-designed or rare surviving public-realm object with its own provenance.
Exceptional transit entrances, public clocks, drinking-water points, sanitary structures and civic measurement, datum or boundary instruments.
An exact object or access pin and current pavement, public-garden or operating-transit visibility.
exclude: Generic benches, lamps, bollards, news kiosks, sanisettes, Morris columns and standard Metro surrounds.
Serial membership alone: retain at most one representative for a genuinely distinct surviving model or provenance.
Sculptural or commemorative fountains whose primary identity is monumental; use monument.
Ordinary plaques, painted advertisements, façades, full station interiors and isolated artworks better classed as plaque, ghostsign, historicshopfronts, stations or streetart.
Objects behind private or access-unverified gates.

why_existing_categories_fail.oddity: Oddity explains strangeness but not the designed civic function.
why_existing_categories_fail.monument: Monument is commemorative or sculptural; these objects were made to perform a recurring urban service.
why_existing_categories_fail.history: History cannot expose this globally repeatable public-interface lens.
why_existing_categories_fail.industrial: Industrial covers system-scale infrastructure rather than the small object a pedestrian directly uses or reads.

global_reuse: London cabmen's shelters, historic urinals and drinking fountains
Vienna Stadtbahn entrances and public clocks
New York subway entrances and street clocks
streetfurniture.metro_boundary: An architect-designed entrance object may be streetfurniture. A remarkable station interior or engineering ensemble must never be nested here; that is a future separate stations category.

historicshopfronts.label: Historic shopfronts
historicshopfronts.definition: A named or individually documented historic retail or trade frontage whose surviving purpose-built exterior fabric is itself the pavement-visible objective.
include: A surviving historic frame, glazing, mosaic, relief, trade image, lettering integrated into the frontage, or fitted exterior detail.
The former trade is materially legible and the facade can be inspected from public pavement without entering the present premises.
A protected frontage or an equivalently well-sourced individually distinctive survivor.
exclude: An active specialist shop, bakery, café or other business where its current offer and walk-in experience are the objective; keep the active-business category.
An isolated faded, painted or applied wall advertisement; use ghostsign.
Generic old-looking storefronts, recreated fronts, private interiors and courtyard-only details.
A whole architecturally notable building where the shopfront is not the atomic objective.

why_existing_categories_fail.ghostsign: Ghost signs are obsolete painted or applied advertising and lettering. A substantially intact three-dimensional fitted commercial facade is a different object class.
why_existing_categories_fail.specialistshops: Specialist shops are selected for their active narrow inventory, expertise and usable retail experience, not inherited exterior fabric.
why_existing_categories_fail.history: History would hide a coherent and highly walkable form among unrelated historic sites.

historicshopfronts.strict_paris_pool_estimate: 10–18; eight all-high protected former-trade fronts are ready as the launch nucleus
global_reuse: London, York and Edinburgh tiled butchers, pharmacies and tobacconists
Brussels, Porto and Lisbon historic grocers and pharmacies
Turin, Milan and Barcelona fitted commercial fronts
Melbourne and Buenos Aires heritage shopfronts
historicshopfronts.same_premises_rule: A current venue and inherited facade may coexist only when both are independently strong and their stories and interactions are explicitly different; otherwise keep one atomic row.

deferred_category_hypotheses.label: Remarkable stations
deferred_category_hypotheses.verdict: defer but keep separate from streetfurniture
deferred_category_hypotheses.reason: A station interior and engineering ensemble is a place-scale experience. Only a discrete exceptional entrance object belongs in streetfurniture.
The live monument label explicitly covers monuments and fountains. Use monument for sculptural fountains and streetfurniture only for exceptional working civic water objects.
The strict current public-experience pool is small and already fits music; Au Lapin Agile is correctly music. Revisit only after a cross-city pool proves consistent.
Use specialistshops for public-facing living trades unless making is directly observable and documented; appointment-only ateliers fail accidental discovery.
Individual bouquiniste boxes are serial, weather-dependent and weakly named. Keep one well-pinned quay ensemble under market rather than padding dozens of boxes.

Notre-Dame-des-Victoires as a devotional rather than generic church objective

collision_and_quality_risks: Do not retag or duplicate Cour du Commerce Saint-André as arcades; it is open-air.
Galerie Vivienne and Librairie Jousseaume are a route and a business, respectively; their nested relationship is explicit and both can survive.
Passage du Bourg-l'Abbé is about 103 m from Passage du Grand-Cerf but has separate entrances, geometry and a distinct sculpted Commerce/Industry story.
A future Passage Jouffroy row must explicitly distinguish the full route from live Galerie Fayet inside it.

Abbesses's Guimard entrance is a genuinely separate object from Le Mur des Je t'aime, but it remains deferred because the roughly 24 m separation breaches this run's non-overridable under-30 m density rule.
The wall-mounted Wallace fountain is close to Fontaine Cuvier and a Jardin des Plantes cedar; public water utility, monumental fountain and living tree are distinct.
Never multiply standard Guimard entrances, Wallace fountains or other serial objects merely to raise count.
Reject stale coordinate sources when they contradict the named object and address; Porte Dauphine and Kiosque des Noctambules both produced such false pins during research.
Do not import the generic live fontainewallace2 row as a category seed until its identity and coordinate are repaired.
Chez Julien's inherited bakery front and La Caféothèque 62 m away are separate; the former is exterior fabric and the latter is an active coffee destination.
A protected historic shopfront is not a ghost sign unless the atomic objective is specifically obsolete painted or applied advertising rather than the fitted frontage.
